about:
Amish Heirlooms Furniture was founded in 2003 by Travis and Jackie Olson in Mason City, Iowa. The family-owned business began after the couple encountered Amish craftsmanship on fishing trips to southeastern Minnesota, inspiring them to open a store dedicated to handcrafted solid-wood furniture. The company has since relocated and expanded four times, with its current showroom located in Clear Lake, Iowa.

The retailer specializes in made-to-order Amish furniture built by individual Amish families in Indiana. Each piece is constructed from solid wood and can be customized to fit a customer’s style and space. Product lines span bedroom, living room, dining room, office, and outdoor furniture, as well as home decor. In addition, the company operates America’s Mattress at the same location, offering pocketed-coil, memory-foam, and latex mattresses with cooling and pressure-relief technologies.

Amish Heirlooms serves residential customers primarily across Iowa, Minnesota, and the broader Midwest. Its showroom in Clear Lake welcomes walk-in shoppers, while the made-to-order model allows families to specify dimensions, wood species, and finishes for pieces such as dining tables, bedroom sets, and outdoor chairs.

The Olsons founded the business on a respect for traditional joinery and a desire to bring heirloom-quality furniture to the region. The company backs its outdoor line with a 100-year promise, emphasizing durability and generational longevity as core differentiators.

name: Amperage Electrical Supply
old_description: Amperage Electrical Supply Inc is your Full Line, Independent, Electrical Supplier serving the Chicagoland area.
about:
Amperage Electrical Supply Inc. has operated as a full-line independent electrical distributor from its base in Roselle, Illinois, since its founding in 1997. The privately held company serves the broader Chicagoland region with a focus on responsive service and broad product availability across the electrical trade.

The distributor maintains an extensive inventory organized around dedicated lighting and switchgear departments, supported by a large fleet of delivery trucks that enables rapid fulfillment throughout its service area. Its product range spans the full spectrum of electrical supplies needed by contractors, from conduit and wire to controls and fixtures.

Amperage primarily serves electrical contractors, commercial builders, and industrial maintenance teams across the Chicago metropolitan area. The company's local presence and stock depth allow it to support both scheduled projects and emergency requirements with same-day delivery capability within its coverage zone.

The business was built on customer service, emphasizing experienced staff, competitive pricing, and a delivery network designed to keep job sites moving. Those pillars remain the stated differentiators in a market where availability and speed often determine project success.

name: Amphenol Industrial Operations
old_description: High-reliability power/signal connectors, cable assemblies, and junction boxes
about:
Amphenol Industrial Operations is headquartered in Endicott, New York. The division operates as part of Amphenol Corporation, a global interconnect manufacturer. No founding year or founder names are disclosed in public materials.

The company produces circular power and signal connectors, cable assemblies, junction boxes, and value‑added box builds. Its portfolio includes proprietary RADSOK® contact technology for high‑amperage applications, ruggedized circular and rectangular interconnects, and board‑level contacts such as the GT, AC, PT, Amphe‑Lite, PowerBlok, SurLok Plus, ePower, UPC, H4 Plus, and UPT series. Over 2,500 employees work across eight manufacturing sites in North America, Asia‑Pacific, Europe, and the Middle East, supporting custom‑engineered cable assemblies and overmolded harnesses.

Customers span alternative energy (including solar), heavy equipment, energy storage, factory automation, eMobility, rail mass transit, datacom/telecom, data‑center power, and power distribution. The company supplies OEMs requiring harsh‑environment interconnects for diesel‑engine vehicles, battery and fuel‑cell systems, locomotives, and high‑density server power.

Amphenol Industrial emphasizes its global manufacturing footprint, regional technical and sales support, and design capabilities for harsh‑environment reliability as key differentiators.

name: Amprius Technologies
about:
Amprius Technologies was founded in 2008 in Fremont, California. The company completed its initial public offering in 2022 and trades on the NYSE; it is led by Chief Executive Officer Tom Stepien, who joined the board in 2025. No founder names are disclosed in public materials.

The company manufactures high-energy-density silicon-nanowire-anode lithium-ion battery cells under the SiCore product line. Production occurs at an MWh-scale facility in Fremont, supplemented by GWh-scale contract manufacturing partnerships in China, with plans to expand across Asia and Europe. The operation supports cell design, anode fabrication, and pack integration for high-performance applications.

Amprius serves unmanned aviation, manned aviation, light electric vehicles, electric vehicles, and AI and robotics sectors. Customers include Nokia Drone Networks, which integrates SiCore batteries into its drone networks, and stratospheric platform developers Prismatic (PHASA-35) and AALTO, which rely on the cells for extended endurance and high-latitude coverage.

The company was established to overcome the energy-density limits of conventional graphite anodes by commercializing silicon nanowire technology. Amprius states its patented cells deliver the highest energy density on the market, enabling longer range, faster charging, and operation across a wide temperature range for mission-critical systems.

about:
Andersen Self-Service Auto Parts operates from Kearney, Nebraska, where it has been based since 1960. The business traces its roots to 1937, when Ray Andersen founded Andersen Wrecking in downtown Gibbon, Nebraska. After relocating to Kearney, the company expanded into metals and vehicle purchasing, later acquiring Stan’s Auto Parts in 1989 to launch Andersen Auto Parts, a discount outlet for classic and older-model vehicle components.

In 2009, the company transformed its property into a self-service facility, crushing roughly 1,400 vehicles to make room for an inventory that now exceeds 1,700 cars, trucks, campers, and motorcycles. Customers bring their own tools and remove the parts they need, a model that allows the company to offer prices up to 80 percent below conventional auto-parts retailers. The yard is organized by vehicle make and model, and staff provide parts-interchange assistance to ensure the correct component is located. The inventory spans vehicles from the 1940s through the mid-2000s.

The operation serves retail customers, classic-car restorers, motorcycle enthusiasts, and independent repair shops seeking affordable used components. While the primary clientele is individual vehicle owners, the breadth of inventory also supports professional mechanics looking for discontinued or hard-to-find parts.

The shift to self-service was driven by a desire to pass maximum savings to customers; by eliminating the labor cost of part removal, the company can maintain low prices while keeping the facility clean, organized, and safe.

about:
Angel Factory operates from Garland, Texas, in the Dallas metropolitan area. The company has been producing apparel since the early 1990s as a full-service sewing contractor. No founders or ownership structure are disclosed in public materials.

The shop handles all types of men's, women's, and children's clothing, offering in-house design, fabric cutting, reworking, embroidery, finishing, and packaging. It works with a broad range of textiles including cotton, knits, wovens, fleece, lycra, cotton lace, rayon, polyester, and pima cotton. Facility size, headcount, and annual volume are not published.

Angel Factory serves fashion designers and wholesalers who need cut-and-sew production for their lines. The company emphasizes that it accepts orders of any size, stating that no client is too big or too small.

The business positions itself on quality and breadth of service, promoting a one-stop experience from design through finished, packaged goods. It highlights the trust of multiple designers and wholesalers as evidence of its reliability.

about:
Apex Textile Company operates from Atlanta, Georgia, bringing over 15 years of industry experience to the institutional textile market. The company was established to serve healthcare, hospitality, industrial, and automotive sectors with a focus on customer satisfaction and product quality.

The company sources and supplies a broad range of textile products, including healthcare linens such as pillowcases, sheets, towels, and blankets; hospitality items like napkins, table tops, and bathroom amenities; industrial textiles such as barmops, shop towels, and aprons; and microfiber products. All products are imported from fabric manufacturers worldwide, allowing Apex to offer a variety of materials including cotton, microfiber, denim, and twill.

Apex serves hospitals, hotels, industrial facilities, and automotive detailing businesses across the Atlanta area. The company notes it supplies "some of the most popular brand across the city," though specific client names are not disclosed.

Apex differentiates itself by emphasizing customer satisfaction as its primary goal, a deep understanding of fabrics, and a commitment to adapting to customer needs efficiently and competitively. The company states it selects products from the finest global fabric manufacturers to ensure comfort and quality.
